news.summary: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
news.summaryTr: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
news.articleText: Sydney Swans players will not be charged after hotel incident, police say - Published Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said. After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement. Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August. The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking. Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are looking into civil action. "Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday. A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police. A lawyer for one of the women said she was "devastated" by the police decision. Jackson Pannam, of Slater and Gordon law firm, added that the move "does not amount to a finding that the incident our client reported did not occur, nor does it diminish the seriousness of what she says happened or its profound impact on her". John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers, acting for the other two women, told the ABC his clients were "very disappointed and distressed". They would "vigorously pursue" a civil action, he said. "My clients' civil claim is based on a different burden of proof, it is based on the balance of probabilities," he said. Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me". "To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued. The Swans said in a statement that it had been "clear from the outset" that its decision to suspend the players was "separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision". "The Club has commenced a comprehensive examination of its AFL program and is committed to acting on the findings and implementing meaningful change to build an environment that players, staff, members, supporters and corporate partners can be proud of," it said. Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich told reporters it was "not a day for anyone to really celebrate" and "we're still looking very hard at the programme and understanding where we need to get better". He said the club would be doing everything to "restore the standards that this club has held for a long period of time". In a separate statement the AFL acknowledged the police decision and said it reserved the right to investigate should any further relevant information come to light.

news.articleText: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI - Published State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say. More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman. This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company. US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction. A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims. Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities. The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user". "It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

news.summary: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.

news.titleTr: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
news.summaryTr: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
news.articleText: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks - Published Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia. European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations. Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed. The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war. But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but further details like how many prisoners would be exchanged or a timeline, were not given. - US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow - Published8 hours ago - Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine - Published14 hours ago Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union. On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important." He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it is to have European delegates "at the table". "He's willing to give it a try," Kushner added. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Earlier on Thursday, Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, told BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player". Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal. Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of Euro leaders gathered in the Irish capital on Thursday that he believed the security of the region has been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war. "Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine remains under control of Russian forces, and cross-border incursions are increasingly common. Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky. Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The technology owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company has played a vital role in government and military connectivity in Ukraine, and increasingly assists in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

news.title: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
news.summary: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
news.summaryTr: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
news.articleText: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over? - Published Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment. "People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC. After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter. "Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion. Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next." Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022. But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force. Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements. Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority. Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat. "The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage." Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says. Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost. Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC. He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy." The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability. It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored. Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes. Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days. "We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active. Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents. The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds. Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded. Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC. Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations. However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael. Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF." He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says. Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says. What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded." While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours." In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict. "First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF." Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade. Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement. In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters. "If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says. Hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says. Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government. However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence. In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace. "Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force. Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements. Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority. Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat. "The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage." Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says. Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost. Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC. He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy." The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability. It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored. Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes. Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days. "We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active. Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents. The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds. Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded. Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC. Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations. However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael. Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF." He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says. Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says. What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded." While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours." In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict. "First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF." Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade. Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement. In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters. "If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says. Hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says. Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government. However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence. In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace. "Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle. items.articleText: Dünyanın en büyük dijital varlık şirketi altınlarını saydırdı: 25,7 tonluk rezerv kanıtlandı - KPMG'nin denetiminde XAUT'yi destekleyen her bir altın külçesinin fiziksel varlığı ve tanımlayıcı bilgileri doğrulandı. Dünyanın en büyük dijital varlık şirketi Tether, Eylül 2026 sonunda XAUT rezervlerinin 3,44 milyar dolar değerinde olduğunu açıkladı. Dünyanın en büyük dijital varlık şirketi Tether, altına dayalı dijital varlığı Tether Gold'un (XAUT) mali tablolarına ilişkin bağımsız denetimin KPMG tarafından tamamlandığını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Yapılan açıklamaya göre denetim, 31 Aralık 2025'te sona eren yıla ait mali tabloları kapsadı. Tether, denetim sonucunda XAUT'nin tamamen tahsis edilmiş fiziki altınla desteklendiğinin doğrulandığını bildirdi. Şirket, KPMG'nin denetim kapsamında dijital varlığı destekleyen her bir altın külçesini fiziksel olarak saydığını ve incelediğini açıkladı. Açıklamada, doğrulamanın yalnızca saklama kuruluşunun onaylarına dayanmadığı, her bir külçenin fiziksel varlığının ve tanımlayıcı bilgilerinin ayrı ayrı kontrol edildiği belirtildi. Tether Finans Direktörü Simon McWilliams, denetimin şirketin finans ekibi açısından yeni bir dönüm noktası olduğunu söyledi. McWilliams, ağustos ayında bugüne kadar gerçekleştirilen en büyük ilk denetimlerden birini tamamladıklarını, son denetimle birlikte fiziksel altına dayalı bilançoları için de ikinci olumlu görüşü aldıklarını ifade etti. McWilliams, şirketin denetim stratejisinin USDT ve XAUT gibi en büyük ve en karmaşık işletmelerden başlayarak sektör için standart oluşturmak üzerine kurulduğunu belirtti. Tether Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Paolo Ardoino ise XAUT'nin geliştirilmesinde önemli bir aşamaya ulaşılmasına rağmen dijital altın uygulamalarının henüz başlangıç aşamasında olduğunu söyledi. Ardoino, XAUT'nin altın borsa yatırım fonu (ETF) piyasasına gerçek anlamda rakip olabilecek ilk platform olduğuna inandıklarını belirtti. Blockchain teknolojisinin altının hızlı transfer edilmesine ve ödemelerde kullanılmasına imkan tanıdığını ifade eden Ardoino, bu teknolojinin daha düşük saklama maliyetleri ve daha yüksek şeffaflık gibi avantajlar sunduğunu kaydetti. Tether'ın USDT ile ölçeklenebilir bir model ortaya koyduğunu belirten Ardoino, aynı modeli altın piyasasına genişletmeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi. XAUT rezervleri 2026'nın ilk dokuz ayında büyümesini sürdürdü. Tether'ın açıklamasına göre, dijital varlığı destekleyen altın miktarı bu dönemde yüzde 59 artarak eylül ayı sonunda 25,7 tona ulaştı. Şirket, söz konusu rezervlerin toplam değerini 3,44 milyar dolar olarak açıkladı. Bununla birlikte Tether, kasım ayının başında yayımladığı üçüncü çeyrek raporunda yaz aylarında fiziksel altın rezervlerinde düşüş yaşandığını bildirdi. USDT rezervlerinde tutulan altın da dahil olmak üzere şirketin toplam altın varlıkları, üçüncü çeyrekte yaklaşık 3 metrik ton azalarak 165 tona geriledi. Tether'ın toplam altın varlıkları haziran sonunda 168 ton seviyesindeydi. Söz konusu düşüş, şirketin ikinci çeyrekte yaklaşık 14 ton altın satın almasının ardından gerçekleşti. Dijital altın piyasasının gelişimine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulunan Dünya Altın Konseyi (WGC) de geçen ay yayımladığı raporda, dijital inovasyonun altının geleneksel değer saklama işlevinin ötesinde kullanım alanları oluşturduğunu belirtti. Konsey, sektörün yeni bir dönüm noktasına yaklaştığını kaydetti. WGC raporunda, sektör paydaşlarının benimsenmenin önündeki temel engelleri aşması halinde 700 milyar dolara kadar potansiyel talebin ortaya çıkabileceği belirtildi. Bu talebin gerçekleşmesi durumunda, dijital altın piyasasının mevcut fiziki altın destekli ETF piyasasına büyük ölçüde eşdeğer bir büyüklüğe ulaşabileceği ifade edildi.

items.title: Bitcoin üç ayın dibinde: Altcoinlerde kayıplar yüzde 7'yi aştı
items.summary: Bitcoin, 69 bin doların altına gerileyerek 19 Ağustos'tan bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Yılın son çeyreğinde yüzde 17 değer kaybeden Bitcoin'deki satış dalgası altcoinlere de yayıldı. Ethereum 2 bin doların, Solana ise 80 doların altına indi.

items.summaryTr: Bitcoin, 69 bin doların altına gerileyerek 19 Ağustos'tan bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Yılın son çeyreğinde yüzde 17 değer kaybeden Bitcoin'deki satış dalgası altcoinlere de yayıldı. Ethereum 2 bin doların, Solana ise 80 doların altına indi.
items.articleText: Bitcoin üç ayın dibinde: Altcoinlerde kayıplar yüzde 7'yi aştı Bitcoin, 69 bin doların altına gerileyerek 19 Ağustos'tan bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Yılın son çeyreğinde yüzde 17 değer kaybeden Bitcoin'deki satış dalgası altcoinlere de yayıldı. Ethereum 2 bin doların, Solana ise 80 doların altına indi. Kripto para piyasasında satış baskısı giderek derinleşiyor. Son dönemde düşüş eğiliminin hakim olduğu piyasada Bitcoin, yaklaşık üç ayın en düşük seviyesine gerilerken, piyasa değeri yüksek diğer kripto para birimlerinde de kayıplar hız kazandı. CoinDesk verilerine göre, piyasa değeri bakımından dünyanın en büyük kripto para birimi Bitcoin, 69 bin doların altına kadar gerileyerek 19 Ağustos'tan bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Bitcoin'de önceki çeyreğin kazançları eriyor Bitcoin'in yılın son çeyreğindeki değer kaybı yüzde 17'ye ulaştı. Son üç aylık dönemde yaşanan düşüş, yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde kaydedilen yükselişin büyük bölümünü tersine çevirdi. Önceki çeyrekte elde ettiği kazanımların önemli bir kısmını geri veren Bitcoin'de satış baskısı sürerken, fiyatın 70 bin doların altına gerilemesi dikkat çekti. Ethereum 2 bin doların altına indi Kripto para piyasasındaki düşüş Bitcoin ile sınırlı kalmadı. Piyasa değeri bakımından ikinci en büyük kripto para birimi Ethereum da satış dalgasından etkilendi. Ethereum, ağustos ayından bu yana ilk kez 2 bin dolar seviyesinin altına geriledi. Ether'in fiyatı 1.925,32 dolara kadar düşerken, diğer büyük kripto para birimlerinde de önemli fiyat eşiklerinin altına inildi. XRP 1 dolar seviyesine yakın işlem görürken, Solana'nın fiyatı ise 80 doların altına geriledi. Altcoinlerde kayıplar yüzde 7'yi aştı Satış dalgası, piyasa değeri daha düşük kripto para birimlerinde de etkisini gösterdi. GateToken (GT), Stacks (STX) ve Monero (XMR) gibi birçok altcoinde değer kayıpları yüzde 7'ye ulaştı veya bu seviyeyi aştı.

items.articleText: Dolar 19 ayın zirvesini tazeledi: Fed'den 50 baz puanlık hamle beklentisi - Fed gelecek ay normalden daha yüksek bir faiz artışına gidebileceği beklentisi doların yükselişini destekledi. Dolar endeksi 103,17 seviyesi ile 19 ayın zirvesinde işlem görürken ABD tahvil getirilerinde de sert yükseliş kaydedildi. ABD dolarının başlıca para birimleri karşısındaki değerini ölçen dolar endeksi, Fed'in gelecek ay daha büyük bir faiz artırımına gidebileceği beklentisiyle güçlü geçen haftanın ardından 19 ayın en yüksek seviyesine yakın seyrini sürdürdü. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Endeks, son işlem gününde yüzde 0,05 gerileyerek 103,17 seviyesinde işlem gördü. Böylece Nisan 2025'ten bu yana kaydedilen en yüksek seviyesine yakın kaldı. Doların yükselişi karşısında euro ve Japon yeni değer kaybetti. Euro, dolar karşısında yüzde 0,1 düşüşle 1,1049 dolara gerileyerek Nisan 2025'ten bu yana en düşük seviyesine yaklaştı. Haftalık kaybı yüzde 0,8'e ulaşan euro, Eylül sonundan bu yana en sert haftalık düşüşünü kaydetmeye hazırlanıyor. Japon yeni ise dolar karşısında 159,875 seviyesinde işlem görerek Eylül başından bu yana en düşük seviyelerine yakın kaldı. Kurun 160 seviyesine yaklaşması, Japon hükümetinin döviz piyasasına müdahale edebileceği yönündeki endişeleri artırdı. Japonya Maliye Bakanı Satsuki Katayama, yenin Perşembe günü dolar karşısında kısa süreliğine 160 seviyesine ulaşmasının ardından Cuma günü yaptığı açıklamada, hükümetin döviz kurundaki dalgalanmalara uygun şekilde yanıt vereceğini söyledi. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın ABD'nin İran'la bir anlaşmaya ihtiyacı olmadığını açıklaması ve yatırımcıların Fed'in gelecek ay daha büyük bir faiz artırımına gidebileceği olasılığını değerlendirmesi, ABD Hazine tahvil getirilerini yukarı taşıdı. items.summaryTr: Suudi Arabistan'ın enerji altyapısına yönelik saldırılar ve Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki nakliye aksamaları petrol fiyatlarını yukarı taşıdı. Barclays, savaş öncesi seviyelerin altında kalan petrol akışı ve düşük küresel stoklar nedeniyle fiyatlarda kısa vadeli yükseliş riskinin ağır bastığını belirtti.
items.articleText: Petrol yönünü yeniden yukarı çevirdi: Barclays'ten arz uyarısı Suudi Arabistan'ın enerji altyapısına yönelik saldırılar ve Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki nakliye aksamaları petrol fiyatlarını yukarı taşıdı. Barclays, savaş öncesi seviyelerin altında kalan petrol akışı ve düşük küresel stoklar nedeniyle fiyatlarda kısa vadeli yükseliş riskinin ağır bastığını belirtti. Suudi Arabistan'ın petrol altyapısı hedef alındı Brent petrolün varil fiyatı yüzde 3,3 artışla 95,82 dolara, WTI ise yüzde 2,6 yükselişle 88,74 dolara çıktı. Petrol fiyatları, gün içinde önce gerilemesine rağmen Yemen'deki İran destekli Husilerin Suudi Arabistan'ın enerji tesislerine yönelik saldırı açıklamalarının ardından toparlandı. Husiler, Doğu-Batı petrol boru hattındaki bir pompa istasyonunu, Kızıldeniz kıyısındaki Yanbu kentinde bulunan bir petrol tesisini ve Riyad'daki bir Aramco binasını hedef aldıklarını duyurdu. Suudi Arabistan liderliğindeki askeri koalisyon ise Husiler tarafından fırlatılan iki insansız hava aracının ele geçirilerek imha edildiğini açıkladı. İHA'lardan birinin Riyad bölgesinde, diğerinin petrol zengini Doğu Bölgesi'nde etkisiz hale getirildiği bildirildi. Hürmüz Boğazı'nda tanker saldırıları sürüyor Körfez'de tanker yangınları, petrol sızıntıları ve insansız hava araçlarıyla füze saldırıları enerji altyapısını tehdit etmeye devam etti. İran ordusu, uyarılarını dikkate almayan dört petrol tankerinin Hürmüz Boğazı'nda patlamalara maruz kaldığını açıkladı. Reuters, İran'ın açıklamalarını bağımsız olarak doğrulayamadı. ABD, İsrail ve İran arasındaki çatışma öncesinde dünya ham petrolünün yaklaşık beşte biri Hürmüz Boğazı üzerinden taşınıyordu. Son haftalarda bölgede gemilere yönelik saldırıların artması, küresel petrol arzına ilişkin endişeleri yeniden gündeme getirdi. Ukrayna'dan Rusya'nın petrol ihracat merkezine saldırı Ukrayna, Rusya'nın Baltık Denizi kıyısındaki Ust-Luga liman bölgesini insansız hava araçlarıyla hedef aldığını açıkladı. Saldırıda yangın çıktığı ve yakıt tankları ağının bir bölümünün zarar gördüğü bildirildi. Petrol, petrol ürünleri ve tahıl ihracatında önemli bir merkez olan Ust-Luga'ya yönelik saldırı, Ukrayna'nın Rus enerji altyapısına yönelik son operasyonu oldu. Matador Economics Başekonomisti Timothy Snyder, Rusya ile Ukrayna arasındaki karşılıklı saldırılar ve İran Devrim Muhafızları'nın gemilere yönelik eylemlerinin petrol fiyatları üzerinde baskı oluşturmaya başladığını söyledi. Trump'ın açıklamalarıyla petrol piyasasında dalgalanma ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın Washington'ın İran'la anlaşmaya ihtiyacı olmadığını belirten sosyal medya paylaşımından önce petrol fiyatları Asya piyasalarının açılışında yaklaşık 1 dolar geriledi. Trump, paylaşımında ABD'nin İran karşısında önemli kazanımlar elde ettiğini savundu. Piyasaların yönü üzerinde OPEC+ üretim verileri de etkili oldu. Ekim ayında ham petrol üretiminin, Orta Doğu'daki nakliye aksamalarına rağmen Suudi Arabistan'ın üretimindeki artışın etkisiyle yükseldiği bildirildi. Rusya-Ukrayna görüşmeleri Kremlin'de başladı Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin ile ABD'li müzakereciler Steve Witkoff ve Jared Kushner, Ukrayna'daki savaşa ilişkin görüşmeler için Kremlin'de bir araya geldi. ABD'li bir temsilci, Putin'in bir sonraki müzakere turuna Avrupa temsilcilerinin katılmasını kabul ettiğini söyledi. Öte yandan ABD Enerji Bilgi İdaresi, geçen hafta ABD'de ham petrol, benzin ve damıtılmış yakıt stoklarının arttığını açıkladı. Dört sektör kaynağı da Washington'ın, yabancı bayraklı gemilerin ABD limanları arasında petrol ve diğer emtiaları taşımasına izin veren düzenlemedeki muafiyet süresini uzatmaya hazırlandığını bildirdi. Barclays: Petrol fiyatlarında yukarı yönlü risk ağır basıyor Barclays, petrol fiyatlarında kısa vadeli risklerin yukarı yönlü olduğunu değerlendirdi. Banka, ABD ile İran arasında yakın zamanda diplomatik anlaşmaya varılmasının düşük olasılık taşıdığını, Hürmüz Boğazı üzerinden petrol akışının savaş öncesi seviyelere dönemediğini ve Çin dışındaki küresel stokların düşük kaldığını belirtti. Energy Sigma raporunda Brent ve Batı Teksas türü ham petrol fiyatlarındaki son düşüşün arz ve stok verileriyle tam olarak örtüşmediği ifade edildi. Barclays, mevcut koşulların devam etmesinin bile petrol fiyatları açısından yükseliş riski oluşturduğunu kaydetti. Hürmüz'den petrol akışı savaş öncesinin yüzde 23 altında Barclays'in verilerine göre, 31 Ekim'de sona eren haftada Hürmüz Boğazı üzerinden doğrudan gerçekleştirilen net petrol ihracatı günlük ortalama 9 milyon varil oldu. Gemiden gemiye transferler ve boğazı devre dışı bırakan boru hatları da hesaba katıldığında toplam akış günlük yaklaşık 18 milyon varile ulaştı. Buna rağmen toplam petrol akışı, savaş öncesi seviyenin yüzde 23 altında kaldı. Banka, deniz taşımacılığına yönelik saldırılardaki artışın Orta Doğu'dan petrol sevkiyatlarının toparlanmasını yavaşlattığını belirtti. Ekim ortasında, İran'a uygulanan ablukaya rağmen petrol sevkiyatları kısa süreliğine savaş öncesi hacimleri aşmıştı. Ancak bu artış kalıcı olmadı. Ekim ayı sonunda 30 günlük ortalama petrol akışı günlük yaklaşık 19,5 milyon varil seviyesinde gerçekleşerek savaş öncesi hacmin yüzde 85'inde kaldı. Barclays Brent tahminini değiştirmedi Barclays, petrol fiyatlarına ilişkin mevcut tahminlerini korurken Brent petrolünde uzun takvim farkı pozisyonu önerisini sürdürdü. Bu strateji, yakın vadeli petrol kontratlarının ileri vadeli kontratlara kıyasla daha güçlü performans göstereceği beklentisine dayanıyor. Banka, kısa vadeli arzın sıkı kalmasının yakın vadeli kontratların daha yüksek fiyatlandığı backwardation piyasa yapısını destekleyeceğini öngördü. WTI ile Kanada ağır petrolü arasındaki fiyat farkında son dönemde görülen genişlemenin ise arz fazlasından kaynaklanmadığı belirtildi. Barclays, farkın taşımacılık maliyetleri, rafineri ve petrol işleme tesislerindeki kesintiler ile stratejik rezervlerden yapılan satışların etkisiyle açıldığını değerlendirdi.

Bu strateji, yakın vadeli petrol kontratlarının ileri vadeli kontratlara kıyasla daha güçlü performans göstereceği beklentisine dayanıyor. Banka, kısa vadeli arzın sıkı kalmasının yakın vadeli kontratların daha yüksek fiyatlandığı backwardation piyasa yapısını destekleyeceğini öngördü. WTI ile Kanada ağır petrolü arasındaki fiyat farkında son dönemde görülen genişlemenin ise arz fazlasından kaynaklanmadığı belirtildi. Barclays, farkın taşımacılık maliyetleri, rafineri ve petrol işleme tesislerindeki kesintiler ile stratejik rezervlerden yapılan satışların etkisiyle açıldığını değerlendirdi.

items.summaryTr: Fed yetkilileri John Williams ve Mary Daly, enflasyonun kalıcılığına dikkat çekerek daha fazla faiz artışına ihtiyaç duyulduğunu belirtti. Piyasalar ise Fed'in aralık, ocak ve mart toplantılarında 25'er baz puanlık faiz artırımına gitmesini fiyatlıyor.
items.articleText: Fed'den çifte mesaj: Faiz artışları için kapı açık - Fed yetkilileri John Williams ve Mary Daly, enflasyonun kalıcılığına dikkat çekerek daha fazla faiz artışına ihtiyaç duyulduğunu belirtti. Piyasalar ise Fed'in aralık, ocak ve mart toplantılarında 25'er baz puanlık faiz artırımına gitmesini fiyatlıyor. ABD Merkez Bankası (Fed) yetkililerinden faiz artırımlarının devam edebileceğine yönelik yeni mesajlar geldi. New York Fed Başkanı John Williams ve San Francisco Fed Başkanı Mary Daly, enflasyonun kalıcılığına dikkat çekerek ilave parasal sıkılaşmaya ihtiyaç duyulduğunu belirtti. Williams: Daha fazla faiz artışı gerekiyor CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle New York Fed Başkanı John Williams, ABD ekonomisinin güçlü seyrini koruduğunu, iş gücü piyasasının güçlenmeye devam ettiğini ve enflasyonun kalıcılık gösterdiğini söyledi. Enflasyonun sürdürülebilir şekilde yüzde 2 hedefine döndürülmesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Williams, "Para politikasını doğru noktaya getirmek için hâlâ yapmamız gereken işler var" ifadelerini kullandı. Williams, faiz artırımlarının zamanlaması ve büyüklüğüne ilişkin ise net bir yönlendirmede bulunmadı. Daly: Enflasyonist baskılar ekonomiye yayılıyor San Francisco Fed Başkanı Mary Daly, enflasyonist baskıların tarifeler ve enerji fiyatlarının ötesine yayıldığını belirterek daha fazla faiz artırımına ihtiyaç duyulacağını söyledi. Daly, giderek daha fazla şirketin yükselen girdi maliyetlerini tüketicilere yansıtmayı değerlendirdiğine dikkat çekti. Yapay zeka yatırımlarının da fiyat baskılarını artırdığını belirten Daly, bu etkinin genel enflasyon üzerinde şimdilik sınırlı kaldığını ifade etti. Öte yandan vadeli işlem piyasalarında Fed'in aralık, ocak ve mart toplantılarında 25'er baz puanlık faiz artırımına gitmesi fiyatlanıyor.

items.titleTr: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summaryTr: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
items.articleText: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony. Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December. - How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions - Published12 hours ago - The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal - Published12 hours ago Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. - Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently? - Published14 hours ago Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December. - How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions - Published12 hours ago - The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal - Published12 hours ago Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. - Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently? - Published14 hours ago Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. items.title: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
items.summary: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
items.summaryTr: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
items.articleText: Sydney Swans players will not be charged after hotel incident, police say - Published Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said. After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement. Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August. The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking. Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are looking into civil action. "Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday. A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police. A lawyer for one of the women said she was "devastated" by the police decision. Jackson Pannam, of Slater and Gordon law firm, added that the move "does not amount to a finding that the incident our client reported did not occur, nor does it diminish the seriousness of what she says happened or its profound impact on her". John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers, acting for the other two women, told the ABC his clients were "very disappointed and distressed". They would "vigorously pursue" a civil action, he said. "My clients' civil claim is based on a different burden of proof, it is based on the balance of probabilities," he said. Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me". "To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued. The Swans said in a statement that it had been "clear from the outset" that its decision to suspend the players was "separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision". "The Club has commenced a comprehensive examination of its AFL program and is committed to acting on the findings and implementing meaningful change to build an environment that players, staff, members, supporters and corporate partners can be proud of," it said. Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich told reporters it was "not a day for anyone to really celebrate" and "we're still looking very hard at the programme and understanding where we need to get better". He said the club would be doing everything to "restore the standards that this club has held for a long period of time". In a separate statement the AFL acknowledged the police decision and said it reserved the right to investigate should any further relevant information come to light.

items.summary: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.

items.titleTr: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
items.summaryTr: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.
items.articleText: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI - Published State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say. More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman. This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company. US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction. A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims. Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities. The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user". "It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

items.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
items.summaryTr: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
items.articleText: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks - Published Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia. European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations. Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed. The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war. But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but further details like how many prisoners would be exchanged or a timeline, were not given. - US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow - Published8 hours ago - Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine - Published14 hours ago Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union. On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important." He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it is to have European delegates "at the table". "He's willing to give it a try," Kushner added. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Earlier on Thursday, Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, told BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player". Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal. Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of Euro leaders gathered in the Irish capital on Thursday that he believed the security of the region has been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war. "Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine remains under control of Russian forces, and cross-border incursions are increasingly common. Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky. Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The technology owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company has played a vital role in government and military connectivity in Ukraine, and increasingly assists in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

items.titleTr: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
items.summaryTr: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
items.articleText: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over? - Published Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment. "People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC. After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter. "Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion. Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next." Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022. But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force. Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements. Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority. Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat. "The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage." Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says. Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost. Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC. He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy." The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability. It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored. Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes. Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days. "We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active. Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents. The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds. Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded. Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC. Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations. However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael. Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF." He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says. Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says. What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded." While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours." In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict. "First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF." Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade. Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement. In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters. "If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says. Hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says. Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government. However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence. In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace. "Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle.
